items.name: Martini
items.about: Gin and a whisper of vermouth, ice-cold. The most famous cocktail of all.
howToSteps: Stir the gin and vermouth with lots of ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled glass.

steps: Stir the gin and vermouth with lots of ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled glass.
drink.garnish: An olive or a lemon twist
drink.zero_proof: Stir chilled tonic, a little olive brine and lemon peel.
drink.fact: Bond asked for his 'shaken, not stirred', though stirring keeps it clear.

items.name: Gin and Tonic
items.about: Gin, tonic and lime: crisp, bitter and very simple.

steps: Fill a glass with ice and add the gin.

drink.zero_proof: Tonic, lime and a sprig of rosemary or cucumber is a grown-up zero-proof.
drink.fact: It began in British India, where quinine-laced tonic was drunk to fight malaria.

items.name: Gimlet
items.about: Gin and lime, sharp and clean.

Strain into a chilled glass.

steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled glass.
drink.zero_proof: Shake lime and syrup with cold cucumber water.
drink.fact: Royal Navy sailors drank lime with their gin to stop scurvy.

items.name: Tom Collins
items.about: A tall, fizzy gin lemonade.

Top up with soda.

items.name: French 75
items.about: Gin, lemon and bubbles. Elegant, and stronger than it tastes.
howToSteps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a flute and top up with sparkling wine.

Strain into a flute and top up with sparkling wine.
drink.zero_proof: Shake lemon and syrup, then top with sparkling white grape juice.

items.name: Sidecar
items.about: Brandy, orange and lemon with a sugared rim.

Strain into a glass with a sugared rim.

drink.zero_proof: Shake lemon and orange juice with cold black tea and a little honey.
drink.fact: It's said to be named after a soldier who rode to his Paris bar in a motorcycle sidecar.

items.name: Kir Royale
items.about: Sparkling wine blushed with blackcurrant.

Top up with sparkling wine.

drink.fact: It's named after Félix Kir, a priest and mayor of Dijon who served it to guests.

items.name: Mimosa

items.name: Old Fashioned
items.about: Whisky, sugar and bitters: the 'old-fashioned' way to drink a cocktail.

Strain over a large ice cube.

drink.fact: Drinkers in the 1880s asked for cocktails made the old-fashioned way, and the name stuck.

items.name: Manhattan

items.name: Mint Julep
